blocks.content: The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30' E, which passes through Mirzapur and is taken as the standard time for the entire country.

rows: Determined by the noon position of the Sun at a specific meridian.
Determined by a central meridian chosen for an entire country or zone.
Differs from place to place across different longitudes.
Uniform throughout the entire country or time zone.
Impractical for national transport, communication, and scheduling.
Essential for synchronized transport schedules, broadcasts, and administration.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on the 82°30' E longitude, passing through Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh.
India's longitudinal span of nearly 30° creates a natural time difference of about 2 hours between Kibithu in Arunachal Pradesh and Guhar Moti in Gujarat.
The Standard Meridian passes through five Indian states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.
1 degree of longitude corresponds to a time difference of 4 minutes.
Exams frequently ask to identify which states the Standard Meridian passes through (UP, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh).
Calculate time variations using the rule: 1° longitude = 4 minutes (15° = 1 hour).
Remember that IST is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (UTC+5:30).
